title: Betamethasone meniscal infiltration under ultrasound control: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter trial.
official: Efficacy of ultrasound-monitored meniscal wall betamethasone infiltration on pain in relation to degenerative meniscal injury: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter trial. MINUS (Meniscal INfiltration of corticosteroid guided with Ultra Sonography)
summary: Main objective: The main objective is to evaluate the efficacy of ultrasound-guided meniscal wall infiltration of betamethasone versus ultrasound-guided meniscal wall infiltration of placebo, at 1 month, on meniscal pain in the treatment of meniscal pain of degenerative origin in adult.

interventions.name: CHLORHYDRATE DE LIDOCAINE RENAUDIN 10 mg/ml, solution injectable
DIPROSTENE, suspension injectable en seringue pré-remplie

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patient aged ≥ 18 years
2. Localized knee pain with tenderness over the medial or lateral joint space reproduced on clinical examination
3. Pain assessed with a VAS score > 4/10 despite first-line medical treatment including the use of tier I or II analgesics or NSAIDs
4. An MRI of the knee performed in the 6 months preceding the operation as part of the pre-treatment assessment
5. Medial or lateral degenerative meniscal lesion on MRI consistent with pain, confirmed by an investigating physician
6. Affiliation to the Social Security
7. Free and informed consent signed by the patient
Exclusion criteria:
1. Patient under 18 years of age
2. History of corticosteroid injection in the knee concerned in the 3 months preceding inclusion
3. Use of NSAIDs and oral corticosteroids during the 48 hours preceding inclusion
4. Use of tier 3 analgesics for gonalgia in the 3 months prior to inclusion
5. Episodes of knee instability or true locking
6. Radiographic gonarthrosis with a Kellgren Lawrence stage > 1 authenticated on radiographic images taken within the last 6 months.
7. Known inflammatory rheumatism
8. Fibromyalgia as determined by the clinical investigator
9. Pregnancy and breastfeeding in progress
10. Contraindication to the use of injectable corticosteroids: septic arthritis, skin lesions at the injection site, severe coagulation disorders, hypersensitivity to one of the excipients
11. Contraindication to the use of systemic corticosteroids: acute infection, untreated and uncontrolled chronic infection, psychiatric or ophthalmological pathologies, unbalanced diabetes, uncontrolled hypertension
12. Patient under curatorship or guardianship
13. Contraindication to the use of lidocaine: known hypersensitivity to lidocaine hydrochloride, to local anaesthetics with an amide bond or to one of the excipients, patients with recurrent porphyrias
14. Patients on anticoagulants
15. Inability to speak, read or write French fluently
16. Patient deprived of liberty
17. Patients with psychiatric pathology
18. Patient who has had an MRI showing an unstable meniscal lesion confirmed by the coordinating radiologist: complete vertical tear of more than 10 mm in length, capsulomeniscal disinsertion of more than 10 mm in length, complex tear, T2 hypersignal tear of liquid type with passage of liquid testifying to the spreading of the edges, tear with displaced meniscal fragment, lesion of a posterior meniscal brake, lesion of the meniscotibial or meniscofemoral attachment
19. Patient with an MRI showing recent ligament injury(ies) (cruciate ligaments and/or collateral ligaments)
20. History of knee trauma less than 3 months
21. History of arthroscopy or open surgery of the involved knee
